standard_prerequisites.name: n-connected maps
standard_prerequisites.statement: f : A -> B is n-connected if trunc n (fiber_f b) is contractible for every b : B.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof compares the truncations of fibers of g and of g o f at an arbitrary c : C.

standard_prerequisites.name: The unstable octahedron identity
standard_prerequisites.statement: The fiber of a composite is the total space of the fibers of the second map over the fibers of the first.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the first equivalence in the displayed chain at source lines 1141-1143.

standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation inside a dependent sum
standard_prerequisites.statement: trunc n (Sigma w, trunc n P(w)) is equivalent to trunc n (Sigma w, P(w)).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the second equivalence at source lines 1144-1145.

core_obligations: Fix c : C and compare trunc n (fiber_{g o f} c) with trunc n (fiber_g c) by a chain of equivalences (source line 1139).
Apply the octahedron identity to rewrite the first term as Trunc n (Sigma w : fiber_g c, fiber_f (proj1 w)) (source lines 1141-1143).
Use truncation inside a dependent sum to move the inner truncation inside, obtaining Trunc n (Sigma w : fiber_g c, trunc n (fiber_f (proj1 w))) (source lines 1144-1145).
Since f is n-connected each trunc n (fiber_f (proj1 w)) is contractible, so the last term is equivalent to trunc n (fiber_g c) (source lines 1146-1147).
Conclude that trunc n (fiber_g c) is contractible if and only if trunc n (fiber_{g o f} c) is, which is the statement (source lines 1149-1150).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix c : C and rewrite the truncation of the composite fiber by the octahedron identity.
Move the inner truncation inside the dependent sum.
Use n-connectedness of f to contract the inner fibers.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 7.5.6 at source lines 1133-1136: if f : A -> B is n-connected then g : B -> C is n-connected if and only if g o f is. The author's proof (source lines 1138-1151) is a three-step chain of equivalences of truncations at a fixed c : C in which each step is a different input: the octahedron identity identifies the fiber of the composite with a total space of fibers (source lines 1141-1143), truncation inside a dependent sum moves the inner truncation inward (lines 1144-1145), and the hypothesis that f is n-connected contracts the inner truncated fibers (lines 1146-1147). Only after the chain does the equivalence of contractibility statements follow (lines 1149-1150). The statement records none of the three steps.
